data.why: The app's primary workflow needs no files at all (built-in synthetic earthquake generator); the two CSVs exercise the single-column and two-column CSV upload paths, including a missing-value row, matching utils/data_loader.py's load_csv_signal format detection.

goals: Generate a synthetic earthquake waveform for a chosen magnitude, depth, and distance and inspect the resulting seismogram
Apply a zero-phase Butterworth bandpass filter to isolate a frequency band and compare filtered vs raw waveform
Run FFT/Welch PSD spectral analysis to find the dominant frequency, spectral centroid, and bandwidth of the signal
Compute an STFT spectrogram to see how frequency content evolves over time (P pulse, S pulse, surface-wave coda)
Pick the P-wave arrival with an STA/LTA detector by tuning STA/LTA window lengths and trigger threshold
Upload a CSV waveform (single- or two-column) and export the processed signal, FFT, PSD, and STA/LTA results as CSV

review.summary: The tree follows the README's workflow (data source, filtering, spectra, STA/LTA picking, reference tabs, CSV export), its features are cleanly cut, and its evidence checks out apart from one mislabelled chart. It needs small fixes before filing: add the S–P/Wadati distance step, correct the Vp/Vs chart label, and make clear that the arrival cards come from the detector, not the synthetic truth.
